source_refs.note: Topic 1.7.5, printed page 12: the trends in electron affinity and Table 1.1.

blocks.text: As the atomic size increases down a group, the larger electron cloud makes the incoming electron feel less attraction from the nucleus, so electron affinity generally decreases down the group; among the halogens the order is At less than I less than Br less than F less than Cl. Across a period electron affinities generally become more negative from left to right, first because the nuclear charge increases and attracts additional electrons more strongly, and second because the atomic radius decreases.
